articles.title: Júlio Mamute, de pesar 310 kilos a participar en maratones: "Eso no era vivir, era estar vivo"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño, que correrá en España por primera vez, cuenta a MARCA los motivos que le llevaron a alcanzar ese peso, cómo ha perdido 120 kilos y su propósito en las carreras
articles.summary: El brasileño, que correrá en España por primera vez, cuenta a MARCA los motivos que le llevaron a alcanzar ese peso, cómo ha perdido 120 kilos y su propósito en las carreras
articles.body: De niño era delgado. A los 18 años ya pesaba entre 150 y 180 kilos. Con la pandemia alcanzó los 310. Pasó dos años en cama y con una máquina de oxígeno para poder respirar. "No era vivir, era estar vivo. Me había convertido en rehén de mi propio cuerpo, rehén de la comida", confiesa a MARCA el brasileño Júlio Otávio Miranda da Silva, conocido como Julio Mamute, que este domingo disputa la Cursa Bombers Barcelona. En su familia no había ningún antecedente de obesidad. Recuerda su infancia como la de un niño muy activo que jugaba en las calles de Recife, en la costa del océano Atlántico del noreste de Brasil, y practicaba natación. El problema con la báscula empezó a los 11 o 12 años, en la preadolescencia. "Más libertad, ir a dormir tarde, comía lo que quería... Fue un hábito que se fue haciendo grande conmigo. Y de adulto fui subiendo y bajando peso durante años", explica. Lo peor llegó con la pandemia. "Terminé una relación el mismo mes en que empezó el confinamiento, me encerré en casa y la comida llegaba por aplicación. En dos años engordé más de 100 kilos y pasé de los 310. Casi no salía de la cama; dormía con una máquina para poder respirar. Ducharme me cansaba más que una carrera de hoy", rememora. Las tareas más cotidianas se convirtieron en un desafío. En la actualidad ha perdido más de 120 kg. de forma natural, con entrenamiento y alimentación. Ayuna por la mañana, come mucha proteína, pocos carbohidratos y muchas ensalada. Dejó los refrescos y los dulces, que ahora apenas prueba. "Después de 25 años de compulsión alimentaria lo había probado todo, hasta un balón gástrico, pero la compulsión me ganaba de tal manera que acabó reventando dentro de mi estómago y tuve que ingresar en el hospital para que me lo quitaran. Cuando toqué fondo, en aquella habitación oscura donde pasé años sin moverme, entendí una cosa: no existe solución externa para un comportamiento interno", reflexiona. El punto de inflexión llegó hace tres años, justo el día de su cumpleaños, el 13 de noviembre. Estaba encerrado en casa, sin querer ver a nadie, sólo su madre fue a visitarle. El nacimiento de su sobrino se adelantó tres semanas y nació el mismo día que él y a la misma hora. "No supe explicarlo de otra manera que como un mensaje muy claro de que la vida valía la pena. Lloré como nunca había llorado". Días después fue a conocerlo a casa de su hermana y a llevarle su primer regalo, un peluche. "No conseguí bajar del coche. Sentí una rabia y un dolor profundo como nunca antes. Me sentí una basura, que nada tenía sentido. A partir de ese momento, el dolor de seguir así pasó a ser mucho mayor que cualquier sacrificio para empezar a adelgazar", cuenta. Ese mismo día se apuntó a natación. Empezó nadando 50 minutos por la mañana y 50 por la tarde. Caminar no era posible en aquel momento, así que necesitaba que la gravedad jugara a su favor. "La natación me salvó la vida. De los más de 120 kilos que he perdido, al menos 100 fueron en el agua. Lo de correr llegó después, cuando el cuerpo ya me dejaba. Lo que siento hoy al recorrer largas distancias es difícil de explicar con palabras. Sólo puedo decirlo así: el ser humano es el animal mejor adaptado del mundo para recorrer medias y largas distancias, y la obesidad me robó hasta la capacidad de dar unos pocos pasos. Por eso me emociono tanto en cada carrera, y por eso vivo este propósito de participar en pruebas por todo el mundo", añade. Hoy nada 50 minutos al día, 4 veces por semana, y complementa los entrenamientos con gimnasio. No le importa la distancia, un maratón o un 10K, ni el tiempo. "Mi maratón es personal: empezó con más de 310 kilos encima de una cama y terminará cuando esté por debajo de los 100. Y mi objetivo es hacer los 42 kilómetros de la maratón original, de Maratón a Atenas, en Grecia", desvela. Su otro objetivo es "inspirar y que otros luchen por sus propias vidas". Ése fue el motivo por el que empezó a contar su historia en las redes sociales. Hoy le siguen más de 5 millones de personas. "Suelo bromear con que es el viaje del último mamut que queda vivo y que se niega a extinguirse", dice. Tiene 35 años. Su primera carrera popular fue la San Silvestre de Sao Paulo el 31 de diciembre del año pasado: 15,8 kilómetros, con unos 220 kilos en poco más de 6 horas. Su primera carrera fuera de Brasil fue el 'Maratón da Europa' celebrado en Aveiro (Portugal) en abril con su camiseta de 'Você pode' (Tú puedes) y su bastón. Después vinieron los maratones en Argentina, Uruguay y acaba de disputar el de la Gran Muralla china. Este domingo correrá por primera vez en España, en la Cursa Bombers Barcelona, una 10K. Será especial porque cumplirá el sueño de su padre, muy fan de Julio Iglesias. Creció escuchando su música y él también es un gran admirador. "Todavía hoy escuchar sus canciones me genera una emoción instantánea. No pude llevar a mi padre a España, que era su sueño, pero pude llevarlo a ver un concierto del hombre del que heredé mi nombre. Al estar en España ahora llevo conmigo ese sueño suyo. Lo hago por los dos", dice. Por cada kilo que pierde, Júlio dona alimentos. Ya lleva dos toneladas a Brasil y en el extranjero. "Lo que me estaba matando, por exceso, va a quien de verdad lo necesita. Es mi forma de devolverle al mundo todo lo que está pasando en mi vida", dice. En España no será distinto, el día 17 hará una entrega de alimentos en Barcelona.

articles.title: El 'Pedroso Team' deja Guadalajara y se instala en el CAR de Madrid
articles.standfirst: El histórico saltador de longitud cubano llevaba más de 15 años entrenando en la capital alcarreña
articles.summary: El histórico saltador de longitud cubano llevaba más de 15 años entrenando en la capital alcarreña
articles.body: Nuevo movimiento sísmico en el atletismo español. Tras las últimas 'fugas' para entrenar en el extranjeros de atletas como Josué Canales y María Vicente -o con técnicos de otros países como Águeda Marqués-, la siguiente revolución se circunscribe al ámbito nacional aunque es aún más importante que las anteriores. Porque la protagoniza nada menos que el 'Team Pedroso', que lidera el histórico ex saltador cubano desde hace más de 15 años en Guadalajara. La noticia en este caso no tiene que ver con la llegada o salida de nuevos atletas sino con el cambio de sede, de la capital alcarreña a Madrid para establecerse de forma permanente en el Centro de Alto Rendimiento (CAR) de la capital española, donde el entorno es mucho mas favorable para la preparación de un grupo de alto rendimiento de cara a los ambiciosos objetivos de 2027 y 2028. Desde el pasado jueves, el 'Pedroso Team' trabaja de forma oficial en el CAR. Iván Pedroso se retiró del atletismo en 2007 con un oro olímpico y nueve mundiales -cinco de ellos en pista cubierta- y en 2010 se estableció definitivamente en Guadalajara por motivos familiares. En todos estos años ha entrenado a saltadores de la talla de Teddy Tamgho, Yulimar Rojas, Ana Peleteiro y Jordan Díaz. Con el técnico caribeño llegan a Madrid, además de la mencionada Rojas, los atletas españoles Fátima Diame, Héctor Santos, Eusebio Cáceres, Tessy Ebosele y Carmen Rosales, el cubano Juan Miguel Echevarría, el francés Erwan Konaté y el portugués Tiago Pereira, que lógicamente también abandonan Guadalajara siguiendo a su entrenador. Cabe precisar que la 'mudanza' ha sido compleja para no perder la continuidad del entrenamiento y preparar el entorno para acogerles. Los atletas debían dejar sus pisos en Guadalajara y establecerse ahora en Madrid. De hecho, Tessy Ebosele y Carmen Rosales vivirán en la Residencia Blume. En cuanto al propio Pedroso, seguirá residiendo en Guadalajara por cuestiones familiares, trasladándose a Madrid a diario. Echevarría, ese descomunal talento que busca reencontrarse con su mejor versión de la mano de su compatriota, hará lo mismo. Para la Federación Española se trata de un movimiento estratégico de vital importancia aunque Pedroso está dentro de su organigrama desde principios de 2025. El objetivo es doble: aspirar a mejorar las prestaciones de los atletas actuales de cara a Valencia 2027 y Los Ángeles 2028, así como trabajar en la orientación y desarrollo de los jóvenes talentos que puedan entrar dentro del programa del CAR de Madrid. El entorno desde luego es el ideal porque en el CAR cuenta con todas las facilidades, empezando por ese módulo climatizado del que carece en Guadalajara. De hecho, ya era frecuente que Pedroso se trasladara a Madrid para trabajar con sus atletas, sobre todo esta última temporada. A ello se sumaba, al menos a veces, la falta de disponibilidad del Estadio Municipal Fuente de la Niña en Guadalajara por su uso festivo para conciertos u otros eventos, lo que suponía puntualmente un inconveniente para el grupo de trabajo liderado por el cubano.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early Predictions for the 2027 Hockey Hall of Fame
articles.summary: We're about seven months away from the big announcement.
articles.body:
We're about seven months away from the big announcement.

Still, a cottage industry in every major sport is perpetually debating choices for halls of fame, and B/R's stick and puck types decided to get in on the action with way-too-early player picks for the 2027 class at the Hockey Hall of Fame.

The public announcement is made in late June, shortly after the Stanley Cup is awarded to and hoisted by the NHL's newly-minted championship team.

The Class of 2026 included Cup champion player Patrice Bergeron and builder Brian Burke, along with Vezina winners Carey Price and Pekka Rinne, 1,000-point scorer Keith Tkachuk, and former U.S. women's team captain Cindy Curley.

We looked at players who've been officially inactive for at least three full seasons, and whittled the list based on each candidate's overall contributions to the game, character, sportsmanship, and playing ability before settling on five.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

Stanley Cup champion (2006, Carolina Hurricanes)

Frank J. Selke Trophy winner (2006, 2007)

It's been more than a decade on the outside-looking-in side of things for "Rod the Bod," but at least the veteran of 20 NHL seasons and nearly 1,500 games as a player has been distracting himself with worthwhile things.

Brind'Amour coached the Hurricanes to the second Cup in franchise history in June, their first since they won it all with him as captain in 2006.

His 1,184 points are better than more than 30 currently enshrined forwards and is the fourth-highest total among players not yet invited to Toronto. It doesn't hurt his 2027 cause that the field isn't crowded with slam-dunk superstars.

It's the first time on the Hall eligibility list for "Johnny Hockey" and it's hard to imagine that Gaudreau won't corner the market on sentimental voters.

His death in the summer of 2024 jolted the NHL and the hockey world as a whole and his presence was felt during the U.S. run to Olympic gold in 2026.

Are his 243 goals and 743 points—topped by 40 goals and 115 points in 2021-22—across parts of 11 seasons good enough in a typical scenario? Probably not. But this is far from typical.

And a vote for Gaudreau is far from an unreasonable one.

Stanley Cup champion (2007, Anaheim Ducks)

Olympic champion (2010, 2014, Team Canada)

When it comes to playing a role in significant team accomplishments, few modern players can rival the impact that Ryan Getzlaf made across a 17-year pro career.

But even though the longtime Anaheim Ducks captain never won an individual NHL trophy, he's emerged as a top candidate for induction as he enters his third year of eligibility for enshrinement in Toronto.

More than 1,000 points amassed in more than 1,000 games played will do that for a player, particularly, as mentioned with Brind'Amour, in a year where there are no can't-miss candidates to take the oxygen out of the room.

Olympic medalist (2010, 2018, Team Finland)

IIHF World Championship medalist (2008, 2009, 2011, 2017, 2019, Team Finland)

NCAA champion (2012, 2013, University of Minnesota)

A maximum of two female players can be selected for induction each year and there's no candidate to join the 15 women enshrined since 2010 who's any more qualified for the honor than Noora Raty.

The 5'5" Finn competed in four Olympics and nine IIHF World Championship tournaments, won two NCAA championships at Minnesota, and had a stellar 2012-13 season with the Golden Gophers in which she went 38-0-0 with 17 shutouts.

She later played professionally in Russia and Canada and was the first female goaltender to play in some of Finland's top men's minor/professional leagues.

Bottom line: If a woman is in the Class of 2027, it's got to be Noora Räty.

Stanley Cup champion (2008, Detroit Red Wings)

He's not made the Hall in five years of eligibility, but whether Henrik Zetterberg ever makes it he's got an armload of impressive accomplishments.

The Swedish forward won a Stanley Cup, an Olympic gold medal, and an IIHF world championship to become a member of the "Triple Gold Club," with Team Sweden becoming the first to grab the latter two titles in the same year in 2006.

Zetterberg played parts of 15 NHL seasons (all with the Detroit Red Wings) and compiled 960 points across 1,082 games, including career highs of 43 goals and 92 points in a 2007-08 run that ended with a hoisted Cup.

And come summertime, it'll be Hall time for "Hank."

articles.title: Gagan Narang, Kamlesh Mehta, Yogeshwar Dutt, Vijender Singh elected unopposed in IOA SOM elections
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections have been reduced to a contest in the female category
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections have been reduced to a contest in the female category after eight of the 12 male candidates withdrew from the fray, leaving the four remaining nominees unopposed.According to the final list of contesting candidates issued by the Electoral Officer (RO) Sanjay K Srivastava on Saturday, Gagan Narang, Kamlesh Mehta, Yogeshwar Dutt and Vijender Singh will be elected unopposed to the four male positions. With the number of candidates matching the number of available seats, the November 9 election in the male category will serve no purpose.The female category, however, will see a contest, with six candidates vying for four positions. The final list comprises Dola Banerjee, current IOA president PT Usha, Rani Rampal, Saina Nehwal, Anitha Paul Durai and Anju Bobby George.Of the 12 male candidates who were declared validly nominated on Thursday, the eight male withdrawals include shooter Ronjan Sodhi, table tennis player Achanta Sharath Kamal and former IOA president Adille Sumariwalla.The other male candidates who withdrew were Mansher Singh, Surinder Singh Shokar, Moraad Ali Khan, Sathish Kumar Sivalingam and B Sai Praneeth.In the female category, five of the 11 validly nominated candidates withdrew, leaving six in contention for four positions. Ashwini Nachappa, Chekrovolu Swuro, Neelam Setti Laxmi, Ragina Kiro and Trupti Murgunde were among those who withdrew.The election for the four female SOM positions will be held on November 9. The declaration of results is also scheduled for the same day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IIHF 'taking the necessary steps' to comply with Russia return ruling as Belarus ban remains
articles.summary: The IIHF says it disagrees with the CAS ruling but is taking steps to allow Russia in the World Junior Championships amid a multinational boycott.
articles.body: The International Ice Hockey Federation provided updates on Belarusian and Russian athletes in its upcoming world tournaments, including next month's World Junior Championships. The IIHF announced Saturday that Belarus will not participate, but the federation is "taking the necessary steps required" to comply with the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) ruling to allow Russia to play. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization’s financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the federation said in a statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs, including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey." The CAS ruled last week that Russian teams can compete in upcoming men's and women's world championships, overturning the International Ice Hockey Federation's (IIHF) decisions to exclude them from its competitions. The World Juniors will be the first tournament affected by the decision. Hockey Canada and Prime Minister Mark Carney said last week that Russians would not be allowed to play in next month's World Juniors, which will take place in Alberta. Russia did not compete in Olympic hockey earlier this year, the first since 2014 that had NHL players, nor was it included in the NHL's 4 Nations Face-Off. Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, four days after Olympic competition ended that year. Vladimir Putin put out a statement through the state-run Russian outlet TASS calling out organizations that are preventing Russian athletes from competing for their country. HOCKEY GREAT WAYNE GRETZKY DEFENDS RELATIONSHIP WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP AND SPEAKS ON RUSSIAN HOCKEY BAN "Unfortunately, they have not honored the commitments they once made, and they continue to enforce restrictions against Russian sports that are not based on law, but are instead highly politicized," Putin said, via translation. "This constitutes a clear and gross violation of the law and of judicial rulings — and, by extension, a violation of the very institutions of democracy. That is precisely how this should be interpreted." Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia and Denmark came out with statements signing up for a boycott of games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. Germany, the host of the 2027 men's world championships, also suggested backing out if Russia was allowed to play. STRAUSS, a workwear company that is a top sponsor of the world championships next year, threatened to walk away after Finland announced Monday it was rallying other nations to refuse to play Russia. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER If Russia makes the trip next month, it will be its first time playing in the World Juniors since 2021. It has not won gold since 2011.

articles.title: Taniya scripts history! India's first-ever beach wrestling medallist at Youth Olympics with silver in Dakar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Taniya scripted a slice of history at the Youth Olympic Games 2026 in Dakar, Senegal, on Saturday, becoming the country's first-ever
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Taniya scripted a slice of history at the Youth Olympic Games 2026 in Dakar, Senegal, on Saturday, becoming the country's first-ever beach wrestling medallist at the global multi-sport event after winning silver in the women's 75kg category.The Indian wrestler went down 1-2 to China's Min Zhao in the gold medal bout at the Saly Beach West venue but had plenty to celebrate after a remarkable campaign in a discipline making its Youth Olympics debut at Dakar 2026.Taniya's silver also added to India's growing medal tally at the ongoing Games, taking the country's count to seven medals — three silver and four bronze.The Indian grappler entered the final after an impressive run through the competition, underlining her credentials against a strong international field. However, she came up against a formidable opponent in Zhao, who had won the 2025 U17 World Wrestling Championships title in the women's 69kg freestyle category.The Chinese wrestler eventually prevailed in the final, leaving Taniya with a historic silver medal.Taniya storms into final with unbeaten runTaniya's journey to the podium was built on an impressive unbeaten run in the group stage, where she won all three of her bouts in Group B.She opened her campaign with a 3-1 victory over Germany's Mia Bauer before registering a convincing 3-0 win against Greece's Vasiliki Karavanou. Both opponents had won medals at the U17 European Beach Wrestling Championships earlier this year.The Indian continued her dominant run with a 4-1 victory over Estonia's Merily Vaester in her final group encounter to book a place in the semi-finals.Taniya then produced another impressive performance in the knockout stage, defeating the United States' Matilda Hruby 3-1 to secure her place in the gold medal bout.Hruby had arrived in Dakar as one of the strong contenders, having won the women's 75kg title at the U17 World Beach Wrestling Championships 2026 in Azerbaijan after winning all five of her bouts by fall.Taniya's ability to overcome such a formidable opponent further underlined the significance of her achievement.The Indian wrestler also brought valuable international experience into the competition, having won bronze in the women's freestyle 69kg category at the U17 World Wrestling Championships 2026 in Baku, Azerbaijan, and silver at the U17 Asian Championships earlier this year.India's medal tally rises to seven in DakarTaniya's silver was India's seventh medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, with the contingent having secured three silver and four bronze medals so far.Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada had earlier claimed silver in the women's 63kg judo event, while Tanvi Patri finished runner-up in women's singles badminton.India's bronze medal winners include swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu, who secured two medals in the women's 100m and 200m freestyle events, and Tirthank Pegu, who finished third in the men's 200m butterfly.Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu also contributed to the tally with bronze in the women's changquan combined wushu event.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kao Miura wins men's figure skating title and completes Japanese sweep at Cup of China
articles.summary: SHENZHEN, China (AP) — Kao Miura completed a Japanese sweep with a commanding victory in the men's program at the Cup of China on Sunday.A day after compatri...
articles.body:
SHENZHEN, China (AP) — Kao Miura completed a Japanese sweep with a commanding victory in the men's program at the Cup of China on Sunday.

A day after compatriot Chiba Mone won the women's title, Miura posted a personal-best 190.35 in the free skate for an overall career-best score of 293.25 to build on his lead from Friday's short program .

The 21-year-old Miura finished well clear of second-placed Vladislav Dikidzhi (282.44) and Evgeni Semenenko was third with 281.62. It was Dikidzhi's first career Grand Prix medal.

"It's turned out to be a very happy day for me," said Miura, who finished second at the Grand Prix de France . "It was the best performance of my career so thank you.

"At the last Grand Prix Final I was in three years ago, which was also in China, I ran up a fever and did not perform as well as I could have. This year's Final is in China again so I'm looking to redeem myself."

Miura's compatriot Sato Shun, who won Olympic bronze in Milan , finished fourth on 277.20 after popping a couple of jumps.

Olympic champion Mikhail Shaidorov was fifth on 263.49 and missed out on qualification for the final.

Miura, who fell just 0.06 short of his personal best in Friday's short program, pumped his fist several times as the music ended on his near-flawless Jekyll and Hyde routine, celebrating the second Grand Prix title of his career.

articles.title: Shourya Ambure wins historic bronze, India's first track and field medal at Dakar Youth Olympics
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Shourya Ambure produced a memorable performance at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, winning a historic bronze medal in the women's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Shourya Ambure produced a memorable performance at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, winning a historic bronze medal in the women's 100m hurdles to deliver the country's first track and field medal at the ongoing edition on Sunday.The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best of 13.59 seconds to finish third in the final, narrowly missing out on the silver medal by just 0.02 seconds. China's Zhang Keyi clinched gold with a timing of 13.17 seconds, while France's Anna Peeters took silver in 13.57 seconds.Ambure's achievement was particularly significant as she was India's only track and field athlete competing at the Games. She also bettered her personal best twice on the same day, underlining her consistency and ability to deliver on the big occasion.Two personal bests in a dayAmbure had already set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 13.77 seconds to qualify for the medal race. She then raised her performance in the final, shaving 0.18 seconds off that mark to secure a place on the podium.The Maharashtra sprinter's bronze adds another significant chapter to her growing career. In the space of just 18 months, she has won medals at the Asian U18 Championships, Asian Youth Games and Youth Olympic Games, establishing herself as one of India's promising young hurdlers.Her performance also provided a significant boost to India's athletics campaign in Dakar, with the youngster making the most of her opportunity as the country's sole representative in track and field.India's medal tally reaches eightAmbure's bronze was India's eighth medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, taking the country's tally to three silver and five bronze medals.Earlier, wrestler Taniya had secured India's first-ever beach wrestling medal at the Games, winning silver in the women's 75kg category. She lost 1-2 to China's Min Zhao, the 2025 U17 world champion in the 69kg category, in the gold medal bout. Taniya had defeated USA's Matilda Hruby 3-1 in the semi-finals.Other silver medallists for India include Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada in women's 63kg judo and Tanvi Patri in badminton.Swimming also contributed three medals, with Dhinidhi Desinghu winning bronze in the women's 100m and 200m freestyle events, while Tirthank Pegu claimed bronze in the men's 200m butterfly. Desinghu became the first Indian to win multiple medals at a single Youth Olympics edition, while Pegu secured India's first-ever male swimming medal at the Games.Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu added another bronze in the women's changquan combined wushu event.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PT Usha loses IOA SOM elections; Anju Bobby George, Rani Rampal, among four, come through in six-way race
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Reigning Indian Olympic Association (IOA) chief PT Usha has lost the crucial Sportspersons of Oustanding Merit (SOMs) elections held on Monday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Reigning Indian Olympic Association (IOA) chief PT Usha has lost the crucial Sportspersons of Oustanding Merit (SOMs) elections held on Monday. As a result, she would not be eligible to run for a second term at the top of Indian sport. Saina Nehwal, Rani Rampal, Anju Bobby George and Dola Banerjee have been elected as the four women.PT Usha and Anitha Paul Durai were the two ex-athletes who contested the online elections but didn't find enough support.Ex-athlete Anju Bobby George (53) garnered the most votes in the six-way race, ahead of ex-hockey captain Rani Rampal (50), former archer Dola Banerjee (45) and ex-shuttler Saina Nehwal (43). PT Usha (40) and Durai (6) lost out.The four were chosen by 80 of their peers who had initially showcased interest in contesting the IOA SOMs Elections. The elections were conducted virtually on the right2vote online platform.Earlier, the process for the IOA SOMs among the men went through with Gagan Narang, Vijender Singh, Yogeshwar Dutt and Kamlesh Mehta getting elected unopposed.They all will now eligible to contest the IOA elections, scheduled for December 5, for the president's post.After the defeat in the IOA SOMs elections, PT Usha has one avenue closed to earn a second term as the president of the Olympic body. Another avenue exists if she is nominated to General Assembly by a national sports federation (NSF), which is unlikely.On the eve of the crucial elections and result, PT Usha had lodged a complaint with the Electoral Officer (RO) Sanjay K Srivastava alleging that Dola Banerjee had violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes.In her complaint, Usha objected to a WhatsApp message circulated through an account bearing Banerjee's name, seeking support for the 'New Bharat Panel' and specifically asking voters to elect four named candidates, along with their ballot serial numbers and roll numbers.Usha cited Clause 1.9 of the Model Code of Conduct, issued on October 30, which states that the promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks.She contended that the circulation of the message amounted to targeted solicitation of votes through social media and appeared to fall within the ambit of the clause.The complaint also referred to Clauses 1.2 and 1.3, which require candidates to conduct their campaigns fairly, with dignity and moderation, and show due respect to other candidates.Usha had urged the election authorities to examine the communication, establish the circumstances under which it was created and circulated, and seek an explanation from the concerned persons.She has also sought appropriate action under the applicable election rules if a violation is established, besides directions to ensure a level playing field for all candidates.As a result, the Model Code of Conduct was reiterated by the Electoral Officer before the votes were registered from 9am until 5pm on Monday.Mass withdrawals mar IOA Athletes Commission, SOMs electionsBefore the six women went through the elections and four men came through unopposed, there were mass withdrawals. As many as 13 ex-athletes -- eight male and five female -- opted out, which set alarm bells ringing.Much like the elections in 2022, government involvement has been observed this time around as well. Ex-wrestler Dutt and former boxer Vijender are BJP leaders, while ex-shooter Narang shifted base to Ahmedabad recently. Former table tennis player Kamlesh Mehta, too, is seen close to the government. Among the women, Nehwal, who is considered a strong contender for the IOA top job, joined the BJP in 2020.Before the IOA SOM Elections, the process for the Athletes Commission went through without the need for any votes. PV Sindhu, Mirabai Chanu, Harmanpreet Singh, Salima Tete, Swapnil Kusale, Bhavani Devi, Tajinderpal Singh Toor, Bombayla Devi, Sajan Prakash and Manjeet Singh were named in the panel. Subsequently, Sindhu was named chairperson and Harmanpreet the vice-chairperson, finding a spot in the IOA Executive Council. Chanu and Sajan Prakash, meanwhile, have been elected as athlete representatives to the IOA General Body and will have the right to vote in the IOA Elections on December 5.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: España gana otros dos bronces en Dakar y asegura una séptima medalla
articles.standfirst: La arquera Sandra Pérez y el atleta de 1.500 metros Alex Sangil acaban terceros mientras que el boxeador Pablo Souto (65kg) pasa a semifinales y se asegura el podio
articles.summary: La arquera Sandra Pérez y el atleta de 1.500 metros Alex Sangil acaban terceros mientras que el boxeador Pablo Souto (65kg) pasa a semifinales y se asegura el podio
articles.body: España sigue engordando su medallero en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud que se disputan en Dakar (Senegal), una competición reservada a deportistas menores de 17 años. Los últimos metales han corrido a cargo de la arquera Sandra Pérez y el atleta de 1.500 metros Alex Sangil. Además el boxeador Pablo Souto (65kg) pasó a semifinales y se asegura el podio. Sandra Pérez había avanzado con anterioridad a octavos de final, ronda en la que empezó a competir hoy, despachando a la eslovaca Adela Tollarovicova por 7-1. Ya en cuartos, sufrió más para vencer en la flecha de desempate (6-5) a la francesa Aurane Lapouge. En semifinales no pudo (1-7) con la turca Dunya Yenihayat, a la postre oro, pero en la lucha por el bronce superó a la singapurense Tabitha Ern Lin Yeo por 6-4. En atletismo los españoles disputaban hasta cuatro finales, con varias opciones de podio, aunque a la postre el único que logró una medalla, también de bronce, fue Sangil (3:59.70) en un 1.500 dominado por el etíope Wabi Seblega (3:58.73). Hubo dos medallas de chocolate para el discóbolo Cristóbal Díaz y el atleta de 2.000 obstáculos Pablo Vázquez. El primero, con un mejor lanzamiento de 55,09 metros, se quedó a menos de un metro del podio mientras que el segundo, con un crono de 5:46.05, acabó lejos de las medallas. Además Mónica Galiano fue novena y última en la final de los 400 metros (57.04). En boxeo, Pablo Souto (65kg) se aseguró una plaza en el podio tras despachar de forma clara (5-0) al trinitense Makieve Bellille y el próximo miércoles buscará la final ante el israelí Artur Eytan Prohnevsky. Los dos bronces de hoy son la quinta y sexta medalla para la delegación española en Dakar 2026 tras el oro de Gift Onkurobo en triple salto, las platas de Diego Molina en remo de mar y Graciela Eningo en lucha playa y el bronce de Blanca Pérez en remo de mar.

articles.title: Confidence remains biggest challenge after historic bronze, says Tirthank Pegu
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Youth Olympic bronze medallist Tirthank Pegu believes a lack of self-belief may have cost him an even higher finish in the 200m butterfly event,
articles.body: KOLKATA: Youth Olympic bronze medallist Tirthank Pegu believes a lack of self-belief may have cost him an even higher finish in the 200m butterfly event, admitting that his mindset remains the biggest area of improvement as he targets an unprecedented Olympic final for India.“The biggest area I need to improve is my mindset. I need to become more positive and more confident in myself,” Pegu said after becoming the first Indian male swimmer to win a medal at the Youth Olympics. “I truly believe my medal could have been a different colour if I hadn’t been struggling with confidence over the past month.”The 17-year-old from Assam secured bronze in the men’s 200m butterfly in 2:01.25, days after narrowly missing the podium in the 100m butterfly, where he finished fourth in 54.98 seconds, just 0.27 seconds adrift of bronze.The swimmer admitted that the heartbreak of narrowly missing a medal in the 100m butterfly also affected him before the 200m final. “To be honest, I was really nervous. I was focusing too much on the medal and worrying about disappointing my coach and everyone who supported me,” he said during a virtual interaction on Monday. “During the last 50m, the only thing in my head was, ‘I hope I get a medal’.”This historic feat would not have been possible though without the influence of his late father, Kunal, a district-level amateur boxer. While Kunal wanted his son to take up boxing, Pegu’s mother was worried about injuries to his face. The youngster eventually took to swimming at the age of four, with his father becoming the driving force behind his journey. The road, however, was far from easy.“It was a struggle financially, but he never showed that struggle to me,” Pegu said. “He did everything he could for my swimming. My mother often says that my father never invested in anything else. I was his investment.”Though his father is no longer around to celebrate the milestone, Pegu, an athlete of Inspire Institute of Sport, carries his influence with him as he looks towards the next phase of his career.Pegu’s achievement came shortly after Dhinidhi Desinghu became the first Indian swimmer to win a Youth Olympic medal, making it a landmark edition of the Games for Indian swimming.While many have described this as a breakthrough moment, Pegu believes it is the result of years of groundwork laid by earlier generations of swimmers. “I wouldn’t call it a sudden success,” he said. “Dhinidhi had already competed at the Olympics in Paris and swimmers like Sajan Prakash and Srihari Nataraj showed what was possible. They created the pathway for us.”For Pegu, the Youth Olympics was the culmination of a year-long effort built around a single target. A large part of his development, according to the teenager, has come under coach Sandeep Sejwal.With Sejwal set to retire from coaching, the medal also carried added significance for Pegu, who has repeatedly credited his mentor for shaping him both as a swimmer and as a person. “Sandeep sir feels like family now,” Pegu said. “He helped me not only in swimming but also in life. He taught me how elite athletes think and what it takes to compete at the highest level.”Looking ahead, Pegu also wants to improve in the 50m butterfly and the 400m individual medley. “Improving in those races will help me become better in the 200m butterfly too,” he said.With a Youth Olympic medal now around his neck, Pegu can finally savour a dream realised, one built on the sacrifices of his late father and the belief of those who helped him along the way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sanjay to lead young India squad on New Zealand tour
articles.summary: KOLKATA: After the Indian men’s hockey team cruised to their sixth Asian Champions Trophy title in Mohali last week, the focus now shifts to building a
articles.body: KOLKATA: After the Indian men’s hockey team cruised to their sixth Asian Champions Trophy title in Mohali last week, the focus now shifts to building a squad for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.And there could be no better way to get things started than with the tour of New Zealand, where India will play three test matches as part of the centenary celebrations between the two countries.Led by Paris Olympics bronze medallist Sanjay, the 20-member squad is packed with players who are widely viewed as the next generation of the men’s national team and potential contenders for India’s campaign at the 2028 Olympics.With several seniors from the Paris cycle entering the latter stages of their careers, Hockey India has focused on building depth across positions, and the latest group reflects that approach.A blend of established young internationals and emerging talent, the squad contains players who have already featured in senior camps and age-group international tournaments over the last few years.Besides Sanjay, who has steadily developed into one of India’s most promising defenders, Nilam Sanjeep Xess and Talem Priyobarta provide a young but increasingly experienced defensive unit, while goalkeeper Mohith HS adds valuable exposure from the senior national setup.The midfield features several players long earmarked for bigger roles in the national programme. Vishnukant Singh and Angad Bir Singh have gained exposure in the senior setup, while Rosan Kujur and Venkatesh Kenche represent a mobile and energetic group.The forward line is perhaps the most exciting one. Uttam Singh and Araijeet Singh Hundal headline an attack rich in potential. Along with Ajeet Yadav, Karthi Selvam and Arshdeep Singh, the squad possesses significant pace and goal-scoring ability.Speaking about the squad, head coach Craig Fulton said in a statement, “The squad is a blend of some upcoming under-21 players and the core of the current India A group. These matches come at the right time to challenge the squad with three matches against a solid New Zealand team playing at home.”With Los Angeles 2028 firmly on the horizon, this group offers perhaps the clearest glimpse yet of the generation India hope to build their next Olympic campaign around.The squad:Goalkeepers: Mohith HS, Pawan;Defenders: Talem Priyobarta, Sanjay (c), Nilam Sanjeep Xess, Sharda Nand Tiwari, Anmol Ekka, Yashdeep Siwach;Midfielders: Angad Bir Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Rabichandra Singh, Vishnukant Singh, Manmeet Singh, Rosan Kujur, Venkatesh Kenche;Forwards: Ajeet Yadav, Uttam Singh, Karthi Selvam, Arshdeep Singh, Araijeet Singh Hundal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Grave accidente doméstico de Maria Shurochkina: la famosa nadadora sufrió importantes quemaduras
articles.standfirst: Maria Shurochkina, dos veces campeona olímpica y 11 del mundo, sufrió graves quemaduras en el 32% de su cuerpo al verter líquido inflamable en una chimenea
articles.summary: Maria Shurochkina, dos veces campeona olímpica y 11 del mundo, sufrió graves quemaduras en el 32% de su cuerpo al verter líquido inflamable en una chimenea
articles.body: Maria Shurochkina, nadadora artística rusa dos veces campeona olímpica (Río 2016 y Tokio 2020) y 11 veces campeona mundial, se encuentra en estado crítico tras sufrir un grave accidente doméstico. La nadadora de 31 años fue trasladada de urgencia al hospital con quemaduras graves en el 32% de su cuerpo tras un incidente relacionado con una chimenea de bioetanol en su apartamento, situado en la planta 17 de un edificio de Moscú. Los médicos luchan por salvar a la deportista ante el temor de que surjan complicaciones por las graves quemaduras que sufrió. El canal ruso 'Telegram Mash' calificó inicialmente el estado de Maria Shurochkina, a la que Vladimir Putin le concedió la Orden de la Amistad en 2016 y la Orden del Honor en 2021, como "moderado", que poco después pasó a considerarse "grave". La Federación Rusa de Deportes Acuáticos confirmó la hospitalización de Shurochkina: "Le deseamos a Maria mucha fuerza y una pronta recuperación. La Federación seguirá de cerca la situación y brindará toda la ayuda que sea necesaria". La prensa rusa informa que Maria Shurochkina intentaba reabastecer la chimenea, pero no la apagó antes de verter en ella un líquido inflamable; esto provocó que su ropa, así como los objetos y muebles cercanos, se incendiaran. Durante la evacuación, los residentes escucharon gritos y llantos, y encontraron a la campeona olímpica herida en las escaleras. "Abrimos la puerta y ella salió corriendo hacia nosotros. Lloraba y gritaba: '¡Me duele!'. Al parecer, estaba intentando encender algo; tenía una botella en la mano y esta prendió fuego. Sufrió quemaduras en los brazos, el abdomen y el rostro", relató uno de los testigos a la prensa rusa. Maria Shurochkina logró escapar por su cuenta del apartamento en llamas, pero se encontraba en estado de shock profundo y sin poder hablar antes de ser trasladada de urgencia al Instituto de Investigación de Emergencias Sklifosovsky. Tras retirarse de la natación competitiva, Shurochkina ha desarrollado una carrera en el mundo del espectáculo, participando en producciones de teatro acuático.

articles.title: Casi 20 hospitalizados con "síntomas extraños" tras un medio maratón en California: la policía lo investiga
articles.standfirst: Las autoridades de California estudian lo ocurrido, debido al incremento inusual de corredores que se sintieron indispuestos, pero aún se desconoce si se debió al calor o a otros factores
articles.summary: Las autoridades de California estudian lo ocurrido, debido al incremento inusual de corredores que se sintieron indispuestos, pero aún se desconoce si se debió al calor o a otros factores
articles.body: Lo que debía ser una fiesta del atletismo ha acabado en la apertura de una investigación policial por "circunstancias sospechosas". Ocurrió en el medio maratón de Santa Barbara, en California, donde participaron más de 7.500 corredores. Al acabar la prueba, casi 20 atletas tuvieron que ser trasladados a distintos centros hospitalarios con "síntomas similares de causa desconocida", un número mayor de lo habitual. Eso llevó a la policía a abrir una investigación para esclarecer el origen de ese malestar. Según un comunicado de Cottage Health, "se ha registrado un número de visitas a urgencias mayor de lo esperado, vinculadas a los participantes de la carrera organizada en Santa Bárbara. Así, 19 participantes llegaron a los servicios de urgencias , varios de ellos con síntomas similares de causa desconocida. Estamos trabajando para determinar si esto se debe al calor o a otros factores”. Por su parte, la policía aseguró que "aún no se ha confirmado la causa de los síntomas reportados. Por el momento, no se recomienda ninguna medida específica para el público; sin embargo, quienes se sientan mal deben buscar atención médica y seguir las indicaciones de los profesionales de la salud". De esta forma, tres de los pacientes tuvieron que permanecer hospitalizados y se encuentran en condición estable, mientras que el resto fue dado de alta tras recibir tratamiento. La investigación determinará si fueron las altas temperaturas que se registraron durante la prueba las causantes de estas indisposiciones o se debe a alguna otra razón.

articles.title: No Olympic quota for Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh despite 25m pistol team gold at World Championships
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Manu Bhaker and Esha Singh endured disappointment in the individual women's 25m pistol event at the ISSF World Championships, finishing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Manu Bhaker and Esha Singh endured disappointment in the individual women's 25m pistol event at the ISSF World Championships, finishing outside the medal positions and missing out on Los Angeles 2028 Olympic quota places.Manu came close to a podium finish but had to settle for fourth place in the final, while Esha finished eighth. With three Olympic quota places available in the event, the Indian shooters missed an opportunity to secure their berths for the 2028 Games. Seven of the eight finalists were eligible to claim a quota place.The result came after a successful outing for the Indian contingent in the team event, where Manu, Esha and Divya Subbaraju clinched the women's 25m pistol gold medal with a combined score of 1,761 in Doha, Qatar, on Tuesday.The Indian trio finished ahead of South Korea, whose team of Jiin Yang, Yejin Oh and Dajung Nam secured silver with 1,748 points. Vietnam claimed bronze with an aggregate score of 1,745.Esha spearheaded India's gold-medal effort with 590 points, including 292 in the Precision round and an impressive 298 in Rapid. Manu contributed 587 points (289 in Precision and 298 in Rapid), while Divya added 584 (289 in Precision and 295 in Rapid).In the individual qualification round, Esha finished third, while Manu secured sixth place to book their spots in the final. However, neither could convert that opportunity into an individual medal or an Olympic quota.India have enjoyed a strong campaign at the World Championships, adding several medals across events. Niveditha Veloor Nair won bronze in the women's 25m standard pistol, while Jaypal Malviya claimed silver in the men's 10m air pistol.The men's 50m pistol team of Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh won gold, with Ravinder also securing individual silver.
